source.title: Comparative assessment of federated and centralized machine learning
source.authors: Ibrahim Abdul Majeed; Sagar Kaushik; Aniruddha Bardhan; V. Tadi; Hwang-Ki Min; K. Kumaraguru; Rajasekhara Reddy Duvvuru Muni

record.tranche_reason: Reports training and test accuracy on naturally labeled MNIST under federated data distributions, including explicit overfitting and underfitting results. It uses a different setting from the mapped claim versions and does not test their specific interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own MNIST training and test accuracy results for varying samples per device and label distributions. Results cited from prior work, including large-batch generalization degradation, are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures effects of per-device sample count and label skew in federated learning, which test none of V1–V8. Section 3.3.2 cites prior evidence for large-batch generalization degradation (V5), but reports no batch-size experiment or new argument establishing that effect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the learning findings: single-label devices behave differently from multi-label devices, too many same-label samples can hamper performance, and the single-sample case shows underfitting. The paper also concludes that federated-learning costs depend on model size, aggregation rounds and rounds per day, with deployment an important cost driver.
record.recipe_differences: Federated learning with non-IID, label-skewed device data; compares federated and centralized learning in some experiments. The mapped versions concern different interventions or settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported learning outcomes vary with samples per device and the distribution of labels across devices.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST with single-label devices, 10 samples per device yield comparable training and test accuracy; larger sample counts show overfitting, while one sample produces slow learning described as underfitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In federated learning with per-device label skew, increasing local sample count can worsen generalization, while extremely small local datasets can slow learning.

record.problems: Relevant accuracy outcomes are presented in figures without numeric values in the supplied text. The reported experiments use MNIST and a particular federated setup; the text does not report uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Figure 1 also reports accuracy trends as samples per device and network depth vary, but the supplied text does not specify the sample-count conditions or numeric values sufficiently to assign separate condition rows.

untested.parts: No random-label fitting or comparison with natural-label generalization.
No width sweep beyond the threshold for zero training error; varying depth does not test this version.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or test of local connectivity.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD held-out comparison.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or evaluation of compensating recipes. The large-batch degradation statement cites prior work.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison of generalization-gap rankings.
No identification and removal of memorized examples.

record.verdict_notes: State corrections indicate that these measures cannot determine any listed version, not that the reported overfitting is unsupported. Numeric figure values are unavailable in the supplied text. Figure 1's depth and sample-count findings are already declared in rows_left_out and do not test V2.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fit random labels or compare random-label and natural-label held-out accuracy.
Does not sweep width beyond the threshold for zero training error.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out performance.
Does not experimentally vary batch size under fixed epoch budgets; the large-batch statement is cited prior work.
Does not measure sharpness or other properties tracking the generalization gap.
